title: Taliban
wiki_lead:
The Taliban is a Sunni Islamist political and militant organization which has governed Afghanistan since 2021. Having previously ruled the country from 1996 to 2001, the group was overthrown following the United States invasion of Afghanistan and fought a twenty-year war which ended in their return to power.
Emerging in 1994 as a faction in the Afghan Civil War (1992–1996), the Taliban largely consisted of warlords from the Pashtun areas of eastern and southern Afghanistan. Under the leadership of Mullah Omar, it took control of most of the country and, after seizing the capital Kabul in 1996, established a government which enforced a strict interpretation of Sharia. They were internationally condemned and isolated for their human rights practices. The Northern Alliance continued a civil war against the group and maintained international recognition as a continuation of the previous government.
After the September 11 attacks in 2001, the United States demanded the Taliban surrender al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, who was residing in the country. Upon refusing to do so, Afghanistan was invaded by a US-led coalition and the Taliban government was overthrown, most of the group fleeing to neighboring Pakistan. Following the invasion, the Taliban regrouped and mounted an insurgency against the US-backed Islamic Republic of Afghanistan and coalition forces. After signing a peace deal with the US, the Taliban conducted a nationwide offensive in 2021 culminating in the fall of Kabul, the collapse of the Islamic Republic, and the reinstatement of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.
The ideology of the Taliban is dominated by the Deobandi movement of Hanafi Islamic fundamentalism, along with elements of Pashtun nationalism. It is de facto the sole legal political force in the country, rejecting the principles of democracy and political parties. The group operates centrally under a supreme leader (Hibatullah Akhundzada since 2016) who wields unlimited power and issues fatwas serving both as law and religious instruction. The Taliban has been condemned for civilian massacres, human rights abuses and restrictions, particularly of women's rights, and persecuting ethnic and religious minorities. Unlike al-Qaeda and the Islamic State, it does not hold transnational aims—it remains discreetly allied with the former and is openly hostile to the latter. It is designated as a terrorist organization by several countries, and its government is largely unrecognized by the international community, with only Russia having granted it diplomatic recognition as of 2026.

Etymology
The word Taliban is Pashto, طَالِباَنْ (ṭālibān), meaning "students", the plural of ṭālib. This is a loanword from Arabic طَالِبْ (ṭālib), using the Pashto plural ending -ān اَنْ. (In Arabic طَالِبَانْ (ṭālibān) means not "students" but rather "two students", as it is a dual form, the Arabic plural being طُلَّابْ (ṭullāb)—occasionally causing some confusion to Arabic speakers.) grok_lead: The Taliban is a predominantly Pashtun, Sunni Islamist militant and political organization founded in southern Afghanistan in 1994, emerging from Deobandi religious students trained in Pakistani madrassas and adhering to a rigid interpretation of Sharia law derived from Hanafi jurisprudence. The group rapidly expanded during Afghanistan 's civil war, capturing Kabul in 1996 and establishing the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, which it ruled until the U.S.-led invasion in 2001 following the September 11 attacks, after providing safe haven to al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden. During its initial rule from 1996 to 2001, the Taliban imposed severe restrictions on daily life, including bans on women's education and employment, destruction of cultural heritage such as the Bamiyan Buddhas, and public executions for moral offenses, while deriving significant revenue from the opium trade despite religious prohibitions on narcotics. Ousted in late 2001, the Taliban regrouped in Pakistan's border regions, launching a persistent insurgency against NATO forces and the Afghan government, employing guerrilla tactics, improvised explosive devices, and suicide bombings that caused thousands of casualties. In August 2021, amid the withdrawal of U.S. and allied troops, the Taliban swiftly overran Afghan security forces and reestablished the Islamic Emirate, which it continues to control as of 2026. Russia became the first country to formally recognize the government in July 2025, though it lacks recognition from most nations including Western countries, and faces internal factionalism, ongoing resistance from groups like the National Resistance Front, economic challenges exacerbated by frozen assets and sanctions, and threats from ISIS-Khorasan. The regime has reinstated harsh edicts limiting women's public participation, enforced by morality police, while pursuing diplomatic outreach to regional powers like China, Pakistan, and Russia.
